title: Irony and understatement
description: Understand when Polish speakers mean the opposite, or much more, than what they say.

blocks.text: Everyday Polish is full of irony and understatement, and intonation does much of the work. No pięknie (well, lovely) usually means something has gone wrong. Ale się popisałeś (you really showed off) criticises a blunder. Understatement plays things down: nie było najgorzej (it was not the worst) often means it was quite good. Fixed expressions such as prędzej mi kaktus na dłoni wyrośnie (a cactus will sooner grow on my palm) say that something will never happen.

blocks.translation: Great, just great! We are late again.
Well, that was clever of you!
It was not bad at all.
blocks.note: Understatement: often means it was good.

blocks.text: Prędzej mi kaktus na dłoni wyrośnie, niż on przeprosi.
blocks.translation: Pigs will fly before he apologises.

blocks.text: Nie ma to jak poniedziałek rano.
blocks.note: Ironic, unless you really love Mondays.

lines.speaker: Bartek
lines.translation: Not too bad. I got top marks.

lines.speaker: Agata
lines.text: No proszę, a mówiłeś, że nic nie umiesz!
lines.translation: Well, well, and you said you knew nothing!
